scope: Independent source/evidence review; CPU and offline compiler only. No GPU contexts, backend requests, or service changes by reviewer.
verdict: Promising experimental kernels. Broad automatic/default upstream dispatch is not ready until address ranges, full-model memory and serving results are validated. Existing legacy default remains opt-in safe.
positive_findings: Q4_K group32 scale/min bit packing, alternating nibble layout and FP32 arithmetic match the GGUF definition; Q6_K preserves signed group16 scales and all six code bits.
FP32 scale reconstruction is followed by an explicit precision choice; BF16-pair retains an FP32 sum of partial GEMMs before the final BF16 output cast.
No saved checkpoint conversion or persistent decoded-weight allocation is introduced by the new direct/dequant functions.

Current launch script reuses original-gguf-args.json unchanged and changes only plugin, policy, trace and compiler-cache environment settings. Active process/effective settings were not queried in this CPU-only review.
New padded-weight views are passed only to the stride-aware candidate kernels; legacy CUDA retains contiguous copies.

findings.title: Guard or widen 32-bit address arithmetic
findings.evidence: The decoder accepts N=262144,K=16384. Offline SM86 compilation emits shl.b32 for flattened z, signed row division and mul.lo.s32 for row*stride, then sign-extends results into pointer offsets. Offsets wrap above 2^31 elements/bytes. No large tensor was allocated or kernel executed.
findings.recommendation: Use int64 before multiplying indices and strides, including output/split buffers, or reject every unsafe derived range at the public entry point. Gemma TP2 shapes tested here remain below these limits.

findings.title: Broad rules exceed measured shape and architecture coverage
findings.evidence: Initial/sweep/cuBLAS timing artifacts cover only Q4_K and Q6_K N=5376,K=10752, M in {4,16,256,4096}, while lab policy applies all N/K and intermediate M values. No architecture key or allocation budget is part of selection.
findings.recommendation: Keep the policy explicitly experimental; benchmark actual attention/gate/head and MTP-verification shapes, validate selected tiles on supported architectures, and retain a bounded fallback.

findings.title: Measure temporary memory in the full model and CUDA graph lifecycle
findings.evidence: BF16 decode allocates 2*N*K bytes per call, BF16-pair twice that plus FP32 output intermediates. The Gemma TP2 token-head shard [131072,5376] requires 1344 MiB for one BF16 weight tensor versus 110.25 MiB for the timed FFN shard. Split-K also allocates split_k*M*N FP32 values.
findings.recommendation: Record peak allocated/reserved memory and actual captured/prefill/MTP shapes with 200000 max context, unchanged KV allocation/offload and concurrent workloads; verify scratch lifetime/reuse across replay. Small standalone captured GEMMs do not establish full-model headroom.

findings.state: tile/stride gap resolved; historical artifacts remain limited
findings.title: Earlier numerical timing checks sampled only the first M tile
findings.evidence: Earlier reference code selected X[:8], and odd GPU smoke inputs were M7,N37. Updated probe now samples first/middle/tail rows. Eight new GPU cases compare every output at M33,N129,K768 with padded/skipped W rows, X stride2, nonzero storage offsets and split-K8; all passed.
findings.recommendation: Retain the historical sampling limitation in reported results. Change finite label to sampled_finite or check full-output finiteness outside timing.

findings.title: Freeze complete benchmark provenance and repetitions
findings.evidence: Timing correctly captures the complete chosen function including dequantization and reductions. Results store the direct-kernel hash but not every cuBLAS/decode/dispatch source hash, exact invocation/repeat count, software versions, memory high-water mark or independent repeated timing distribution. Candidate order is fixed.
findings.recommendation: Record all implementation hashes, invocation, CUDA/Torch/Triton and matmul precision flags, multiple randomized/repeated runs and peak memory. Current roughly 10x FFN large-M result is a kernel result, not a serving speed guarantee.

numerical_contract: The fast BF16 path keeps original GGUF codes and metadata, reconstructs weights in FP32, then rounds weights once for Tensor Core multiplication. It changes accumulation/activation rounding versus legacy A8 kernels. Exact packed-weight decoding does not establish bitwise logits, whole-model quality, or rare-loop equivalence.

upstream.recommendation: Account for the existing open kernel bridge before proposing duplicate integration. RTX3090 numerical, memory and serving measurements can add missing Ampere evidence; exact decoding and stride-copy removal may be separable contributions.
